key_insight: Instead of enumerating every subset of possibly-conflicting LTLf properties, the paper computes in a single fixed-point the mapping from product-game states to all realizable goal sets and synthesizes strategies that achieve maximal realizable sets using a fully symbolic representation.
problem_solved: Scalable synthesis for multiple, potentially incompatible LTLf properties without expensive enumeration of property subsets; finds which combinations are realizable and produces maximal strategies when not all properties can be satisfied.
method: Build a product game and perform one fixed-point computation that relates each state to the goal sets realizable from it.
Introduce Boolean goal variables and exploit monotonicity to symbolically encode exponentially many goal combinations (avoiding explicit subset enumeration).
Synthesize strategies that realize maximal achievable goal sets; fully symbolic algorithm (suitable for BDD/SMT-style representations) for scalability.
impact: Makes reactive synthesis practical when specifications conflict or are too numerous to enumerate, enabling robust controller/policy synthesis in complex, safety-critical or multi-objective AI systems.
visual_elements: Diagram of a product game state graph with arrows to sets of realizable goals (illustrates state→goal-set relation).
Flowchart of the single fixed-point computation (iterate until convergence) vs. combinatorial subset enumeration (crossed out).
Iconic depiction of Boolean goal variables + a symbolic data structure (e.g., BDD-like node) showing compact representation of many combinations.

paper_authors: Christoph Weinhuber, Yannik Schnitzer, Alessandro Abate, David Parker, Giuseppe De Giacomo
